Let me explain what we found inside the S analog block and why it matters. Every PM OS transistor sits inside an Nwell.
Think of the Nwell as a swimming pool of positively doped silicon floating inside the substrate. That pool needs an anchor, a connection that holds it
firmly at the supply voltage. We call this an end tap. A small patch of heavily doped silicon sitting inside the well wired up to power. Why does it
matter? Because silicon has a hidden danger called latchup. Inside every COS chip there are parasitic transistors.
Nobody designs them. They come for free from the layers themselves. Two of them sit back to back and form a structure called a thyister. Normally they are
asleep. But if a stray current is injected from a noise spike, from a fast edge, or from radiation, they can wake each other up. The first one feeds the
second, the second feeds the first, and once that happens, they latch. A direct shot forms between power and ground. The chip draws enormous current. It heats
up. Very often, it destroys itself. And the only way to stop it is to remove power completely. The end tap is the defense. It gives stray charge a low
resistance path to escape before the feedback can ever start. That is why the rule says every P diffusion must have an end tap within 15 microns. It is a
maximum distance to the nearest fire exit. Now here is what we found in the comparator. The designers did it properly. They built a guard ring, a
complete rectangle of N plus tap surrounding the comparator core. They punch 68 contacts through it up to the first local interconnect layer and then
it stops. There is no wire from that interconnect up to metal one zero. We check every single one. So the ring is there, the contacts are there, but the
path to the power supply was never completed. Think of it as a well. They dug it. They lined it with stone. They even fitted the grating on top. But they
never connected the pipe that carries the water away. So the well fills and it has nowhere to drain. That is why magic reports two different violations which
are really one single problem. Five times it says an N well contains no metal connected N plus tap and nine times it says AP diffusion has no end
tap within 15 microns because an unconnected tap does not count as a tap at all. The fix is small and it is ours to make. We add the missing VR on the
existing ring and we connect that metal to the analog supply. No new geometry inside the transistors, no change to the net list. We are simply finishing a
connection that was left incomplete. And one thing is worth saying plainly. This chip has never been fabricated. So we cannot argue that it worked before. This
